findings.breaking_input: POST git/refs succeeds, then the PUT of .arc/preview-check.md fails (422, 5xx, a token without contents:write, or the runner killed between the two calls). The branch exists at main's head SHA. ctx.report for it only runs after both calls.
findings.why: The branch is created but never recorded, so the exit plan cannot remove it. On every re-run the ref returns 200 and the head commit is main's, which has no Arc-Launch-Tag trailer. isOurs is false, so scaffold throws FOREIGN_BRANCH forever and the slot is wedged by launch's own half-made branch. This is the pattern "a resource was reported only after a later call succeeded".
findings.fix: Call ctx.report for the branch right after POST git/refs succeeds. In the existing-branch path, treat a branch whose head SHA equals main's head and which has no file as launch's incomplete branch and finish the PUT.
findings.twin_of: A resource was reported only after a later call succeeded, so a failure in between left an unrecorded commit -> every scaffold with two creates: what is recorded if the second fails?

findings.breaking_input: The owner or a bot creates branch arc/preview-check with their own commit, so there is no launch trailer, and Vercel builds a READY preview of it. They run verify, either before apply or after launch has failed with FOREIGN_BRANCH.
findings.why: probe only reads the branch ref SHA and matches a deployment by SHA. It never checks that the head commit carries this slot's trailer, so it returns ok:true for a preview launch did not make. This is the pattern "verify took any X as the proof".
findings.fix: In probe, fetch the head commit and require isOurs(ctx, message) before accepting. Otherwise return ok:false with a FOREIGN_BRANCH reason.
findings.twin_of: verify took any git deployment of the repo as the proof -> every "some X exists" verify: is it the X this slot made?

findings.breaking_input: The owner opens their own PR from the launch-made arc/preview-check branch, or edits the title. An open PR for head owner:arc/preview-check already exists, so list(open.body)[0] is found, not created.
findings.why: The found PR is reported as {kind:"github-pr"} with no ownership test. Teardown then emits close-pr for a PR launch never opened. The ADR says a PR of that name that launch did not create is refused, but the code only gates on the branch.
findings.fix: Only report the PR as launch's when launch created it. For a found PR, check author or title or body and refuse or skip the report otherwise.
findings.twin_of: A project and domain launch only found were recorded as launch's, so teardown would delete the owner's -> every check-then-create: report the CREATE, not the check

findings.breaking_input: The owner pushes a fix commit onto arc/preview-check, or a bot rebases it. The newest commit then has no trailer. Alternatively, an attacker writes a commit whose message has a line exactly equal to Arc-Launch-Tag: <tag>, and the tag is predictable as slug@slot@provider.
findings.why: Ownership is decided by the newest commit's message only, and the trailer is a guessable constant. A legitimate branch turns FOREIGN_BRANCH after any push, and a forged trailer is accepted as launch's. The check does not use the first commit or the branch creator.
findings.fix: Decide ownership from the branch's first commit after main (compare against the base) or from a recorded SHA in resources. Add a per-run nonce to the trailer if forgery matters.
findings.twin_of: Ownership trailers were matched by prefix and by newest commit only -> every trailer or marker check

findings.breaking_input: Between apply and teardown the owner merges the preview PR, adds commits to the branch, or reuses the branch for real work. Teardown still returns close-pr and delete-branch for the recorded ids.
findings.why: The exit plan is built from recorded resources alone and carries no run-time ownership or state check. Executing delete-branch removes the owner's work.
findings.fix: Have each step carry the trailer or head SHA recorded at apply. The executor re-reads the branch and PR and refuses if the head or trailer differs.
findings.twin_of: A teardown step deleted a file by path, whoever had taken it over since -> every exit-plan step: does it re-check ownership at run time?

findings.breaking_input: Vercel project link.repo is ".." or ".", so full = "org/..". The regex `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}` accepts it.
findings.why: fetch normalizes `/repos/org/../git/ref/heads/main` to `/repos/git/ref/heads/main`. A GitHub request carrying GITHUB_TOKEN then goes to a path other than the repo that was validated. The same holds for a repo name ending in a trailing dot.
findings.fix: Reject repo segments that are "." or "..", and require the first character to be alphanumeric or underscore.
findings.twin_of: The adapter path was data the runner trusted: `providers/x/../../tmp/evil.mjs` ran -> every path built from a registry value

findings.breaking_input: An SSL Labs READY response where an endpoint's grade is a string containing a newline or ESC, such as "A\n[OK] forged". The grade passes through grades: eps.map((e) => e.grade) with no say().
findings.why: Provider-supplied strings go raw into verify evidence. Evidence is printed or stored, so a forged line or terminal escape lands there. Elsewhere in the same file say() is applied. The grade could also be a non-string.
findings.fix: Map grades through say(e.grade, 4). Only list grades that are in GOOD, since ok:true implies they all are.
findings.twin_of: Adapter-supplied strings (resource ids, reasons, answerers) were printed raw -> every terminal line that interpolates provider or adapter data

findings.breaking_input: The owner merges the preview-check PR, or its file already matches main. The branch is ours, no PR is open, and POST pulls answers 422 "No commits between main and arc/preview-check".
findings.why: The PR path assumes a diff always exists. After a merge or a squash the create step throws an uncoded error on every re-run, so scaffold never succeeds again and the slot wedges. The ADR relies on the PR staying open.
findings.fix: If a PR for the branch exists in any state (state=all), report it and let verify decide. Or recreate the branch from main with a fresh commit.
findings.twin_of: A rehearsal's gate-3 refusal was terminal on the first run but a re-run read the recorded approval id as pending -> every state the runner treats as terminal: does every re-entry path honour it?

findings.breaking_input: A venture repo whose default branch is not "main", such as master or trunk.
findings.why: The branch source (git/ref/heads/main) and the PR base are hard-coded. A repo whose default branch is not "main" gets a raw 404 from scaffold. The preview is also proven against a branch that is not the repo's production branch.
findings.fix: Read default_branch from GET /repos/{full} and use it for the ref and the base, or refuse with a coded error.
findings.twin_of: Upstream entries were coerced with `String()`, so a `null` id became the hostname "null" -> every value one adapter hands another through state

findings.breaking_input: SSL Labs returns READY where an endpoint is unreachable: statusMessage "Unable to connect to the server", no grade, no details.
findings.why: That endpoint falls into `bad` and is reported as a hard failure "grade none, no HSTS", not UNSCANNED. An unreachable scanner path is therefore recorded as a verdict about the site's TLS posture.
findings.fix: Treat an endpoint with no grade and a non-Ready statusMessage as UNSCANNED(reason) rather than a failed grade.
findings.twin_of: A poll that ran out reported "no run" while a run was still going -> every poll loop's final reason
